title: Leon Bridges Lands Fourth Adult Alternative Airplay No. 1 With ‘Talk It Over’
summary: The single contributes to Columbia Records’ rare simultaneous No. 1s on Adult Alternative Airplay and Alternative Airplay.
contentText:
Leon Bridges scores his fourth leader on Billboard ’s Adult Alternative Airplay chart as “Talk It Over” rises 2-1 on the Nov. 21-dated ranking.

The track rises to the summit with a 10% increase in plays at the format during the Nov. 6-12 tracking week, according to Luminate.

“Talk It Over” is Bridges’ first leader since “Peaceful Place” in October 2024. Before that, he led with “Bad Bad News” in 2018 and “Smooth Sailin’ ” in 2016.

When “Talk It Over” debuted in September, it became Bridges’ 19th career entry at the format. That’s the fifth-most among soloists in the chart’s 30-year history, behind only Jack Johnson (27), Sheryl Crow, John Mayer (26 each) and Beck (21). Among all acts, Dave Matthews Band (including his solo entries) and U2 share the record, with 36 each.

Bridges released “Talk It Over” in August on the second of three four-song EPs that previewed his fifth studio album, Happiness Anytime . The full 12-track set arrived Sept. 25 via LisaSawyer63/Columbia Records. Produced by J Lloyd-Watson and Lydia Kitto of the British group Jungle, it reached No. 12 on the Top R&B Albums chart and No. 74 on the Billboard 200.

“Talk It Over” is also the first Adult Alternative Airplay No. 1 for Columbia Records since Hozier’s “Nobody’s Soldier” in November 2024. While the label boasts 14 No. 1s at the format this decade, it leads the list and Billboard ’s Alternative Airplay chart simultaneously for the first time in two decades, as Dominic Fike’s “Babydoll” (released via Sandy Boys/Columbia/Legacy) jumps 3-1 on the latter. Columbia last ruled the charts together in April 2004, when John Mayer’s “Clarity” topped Adult Alternative Airplay and Lostprophets’ “Last Train Home” led Alternative Airplay. Before that, for Columbia, Primitive Radio Gods’ “Standing Outside a Broken Phone Booth With Money in My Hand” led both lists at the same time in July 1996.
